newsitem.title: TURKEY: Chevron-led venture signs $250 mln Tengiz deal.
newsitem.headline: Chevron-led venture signs $250 mln Tengiz deal.

text.p: A Chevron Corp -led venture signed a $250-million accord with Bechtel and Turkey's ENKA on Wednesday to increase crude oil output at Kazakhstan's greater Tengiz oilfields.
The agreement covers engineering, purchasing and construction activities at Tengiz, the world's largest discovered oil field in the last 20 years, venture officials said.

The TengizChevroil (TCO) venture between Chevron and Mobil Corp targets an increase in production to 700,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the year 2010 from around 100,000 bpd in 1996, a company official said.

"This contract marks another milestone in the continuation of Tengiz. We expect to invest more than a billion dollars over the next three years," TCO general director Nick Zana said at the signing ceremony.
Production capacity is targeted to reach 240,000 bpd by the year 1999.
The $20-billion TCO venture, in which the Kazakhstan government also has a stake, is centred on Tengiz, located on the northeastern shores of Kazakhstan's Caspian Sea.
"As part of the contract Bechtel and ENKA will employ local contractors and develop local manpower resources," Zana said.
Under the deal, Bechtel and ENKA will build an operations centre which will incorporate equipment to separate gas and oil and distribution systems.
Earlier an official from ENKA said about $100 million of the total investment would be made this year and $150 million in 1998.
"The accord aims to increase the oil output capacity at the greater Tengiz oilfields by 30 percent within two years to 11 million tonnes in 1999," the official who declined to be named told Reuters.
Chevron intends to use a pipeline running through Azerbaijan and Georgia to help get output from Tengiz to world markets.
